pageCache.pageTitle: St Philomena's Catholic Primary School - Mission, Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Mission, Vision and Values
Vision
At St Philomena's, we share the love of God every day in everything we learn, do and say.
This simple vision underpins every aspect of school life. Inspired by the life of our patron saint, St Philomena, and the unique history of our school, we are a Christ-centred community where every person is loved, valued and encouraged to flourish. We believe that, by sharing the love of God through our words and actions, we can make a positive difference within our school, our parish and the wider world.
Mission
Inspired by the teachings of Christ and the example of St Philomena, our mission reflects our commitment to nurturing the whole child and building a community where faith is lived each day:
With Christ at the centre, we strive for excellence, act with respect and serve our community.
Our mission encourages every member of our school community to develop their God-given talents, pursue excellence, treat others with dignity and compassion, and make a positive contribution to our school, parish and the wider world.
Values
Our mission is lived out through our three core values. Together, they guide our decisions, shape our relationships and inspire us to grow in faith as we learn, work and serve alongside one another.
“Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord.”
We strive to be the very best we can be. We work diligently, persevere through challenges and take pride in all that we learn and do. By striving for excellence, we honour God, develop our abilities and fulfil our potential.
“Love your neighbour as yourself.”
We recognise the dignity of every person as a child of God. We demonstrate kindness, honesty and compassion through our words and actions, valuing one another and creating a community where everyone feels welcomed, safe and respected.
“Serve one another humbly in love.”
Following the example of Jesus, we use our gifts and abilities to serve others with generosity and humility. Through our actions, we care for one another, support those in need, and make a positive contribution to our school, parish and the wider community.
United by our vision and mission, and strengthened by our shared values, we seek to build a community where Christ is at the centre of all we do. Together, we strive to live out the Gospel each day, growing in faith, serving others and sharing the love of God in everything we learn, do and say.

pageCache.text:
Catholic Community
Steps in Faith
Steps in Faith - Autumn Term
Steps in Faith - Spring Term
Steps in Faith - Summer Term
Supporting Catholic Life at Home
At St Philomena’s Catholic Primary, we believe that children’s faith is strengthened through the partnership between school, home, and parish. We recognise that families play the first and most important role in nurturing a child’s relationship with God, and we work alongside parents and carers to encourage a joyful, active, and meaningful Catholic life beyond the classroom.
Prayer and Spiritual Life
We encourage families to make prayer an important part of everyday life. Through opportunities in school, children develop an understanding of different forms of prayer and are encouraged to share these practices with their families. Whether through morning prayers, prayers before meals, bedtime prayers, or moments of reflection, prayer helps families grow closer to God and recognise His presence in their lives.
Family Faith Development
We aim to provide families with opportunities and resources that help them grow together in faith. Through family events, prayer opportunities, workshops, and activities, we support parents and carers in continuing their child’s spiritual journey at home.
Our hope is that every family feels confident in celebrating and sharing their faith, creating a home environment where Catholic values are lived, discussed, and experienced.
Sacramental Preparation
The Sacraments are important milestones in a child’s journey of faith. At St Philomena’s, we work closely with families to prepare children for key moments such as First Holy Communion. Parents and carers are encouraged to take an active role in this preparation with the church through meetings, prayer, and opportunities to support their child’s understanding of these special celebrations.
Living Out Catholic Values
Faith is shown through the way we treat others. We encourage families to live out Gospel values such as love, compassion, forgiveness, kindness, and service. Through helping others, showing respect, supporting those in need, and making positive choices each day, families can reflect Christ’s example and bring faith into everyday life.
Faith Across the Curriculum
Our Catholic ethos is woven throughout all areas of school life. Children explore Scripture, the lives of saints, and Catholic teachings through their learning, and we encourage families to continue these conversations at home. By connecting faith with daily experiences, children can understand how their beliefs guide their choices, relationships, and actions.
Family and Parish Involvement
We value the involvement of families in the spiritual life of our school community. Parents and carers are warmly invited to participate in Masses, celebrations, school events, and parish activities.
When families and school work together, children are supported in developing a strong sense of belonging and a deeper connection with their faith community.
A Welcoming Community of Support
At St Philomena’s, we are committed to supporting families throughout their faith journey. We welcome conversations, questions, and opportunities to grow together in faith.
If parents or carers would like to explore becoming Catholic, we can support you in contacting the parish and finding out more about OCIA (Order of Christian Initiation of Adults), previously known as RCIA.
If you would like your child to be baptised, or would like more information about baptism and preparation, please speak to us. We are happy to help families connect with the Church and support them through the next steps.
Together, as a school, family, and parish community, we can help children grow in faith and live out the message of Christ through love, service, and prayer.

Catholic Life and Mission
Catholic Life and Mission Policy
Catholic Social Teaching
Oscar Romero Award
At St Philomena's Catholic Primary School, we are proud to be a Participator School in the Oscar Romero Award. This recognises our commitment to living out Catholic Social Teaching through prayer, learning and action, following the example of Archbishop Oscar Romero, who dedicated his life to standing up for justice, peace and the dignity of every person.
The Oscar Romero Award encourages our whole school community to place Gospel values at the heart of everything we do. Through acts of service, charitable outreach, care for creation and a commitment to social justice, our pupils learn that faith is something to be lived each day.
Building on this achievement, we have now submitted our evidence for the Developer Award. This reflects our continued commitment to embedding Catholic Social Teaching across our curriculum and school life, empowering our pupils to become compassionate, courageous and active citizens who work for the common good.
Class Saints
At St Philomena’s Catholic Primary School, each class has a special saint who accompanies and inspires the children throughout the year. These saints provide a wonderful example of faith, courage and love, reminding us that everyone is called to grow in holiness and follow God’s path.
Through learning about the lives of the saints, children discover how they used their gifts, trusted in God and lived out the teachings of Jesus. Their stories encourage us to reflect on our own choices and how we can share God’s love with those around us.
Our class saints also help us to explore the principles of Catholic Social Teaching, showing us how faith can be put into action through kindness, service, compassion and care for others. They remind us that even small acts of love can make a meaningful difference in our school and wider community.
Reception – St Francis of Assisi
Feast Day: 4 OctoberPatron Saint of Animals and Creation
St Francis of Assisi was chosen for our youngest children because he had a special love for God’s creation and all living things. He saw the beauty of God in nature and treated all creatures with kindness and care.
Catholic Social Teaching link:St Francis is a wonderful example of Stewardship: Care for Creation, reminding us that the world is a precious gift from God and that we all have a responsibility to protect and care for it.
Year 1 – St Bernadette of Lourdes
Feast Day: 16 AprilPatron Saint of the Sick
St Bernadette was chosen for Year 1 because she showed great humility, faith and compassion. Through her experiences at Lourdes, she became a symbol of hope and healing for people throughout the world.
Catholic Social Teaching link:St Bernadette inspires us to live out Human Dignity and the Preferential Option for the Poor and Vulnerable by showing compassion, kindness and care for those who are sick or suffering.
Year 2 – St Joseph
Feast Day: 19 MarchPatron Saint of Workers and Families
St Joseph was chosen for Year 2 because he was a loving and faithful man who cared for Jesus and Mary. Through his work as a carpenter, he showed the value of responsibility, dedication and service.
Catholic Social Teaching link:St Joseph reflects The Common Good and Participation, teaching us that everyone has gifts to share and an important role to play in building a caring community.
Year 3 – St Anthony of Padua
Feast Day: 13 JunePatron Saint of Lost Things
St Anthony was chosen for Year 3 because he was a great teacher who used his knowledge and faith to help others. He dedicated his life to sharing God’s message and guiding people towards Christ.
Catholic Social Teaching link:St Anthony demonstrates Participation and Solidarity, showing us that we are called to use our talents and knowledge to support and serve others.
Year 4 – St Thomas More
Feast Day: 22 JunePatron Saint of Teachers, Lawyers and Public Servants
St Thomas More was chosen for Year 4 because he was a man of courage, wisdom and integrity. He remained faithful to his beliefs and stood up for truth and justice.
Catholic Social Teaching link:St Thomas More inspires us to live out Promoting Peace and Distributive Justice by standing up for what is right and working towards a fairer world.
Year 5 – St Paul the Apostle
Feast Day: 29 JunePatron Saint of the Church and Mission
St Paul was chosen for Year 5 because his life shows the power of transformation and the importance of sharing the Good News. He travelled widely to spread the message of Jesus and build Christian communities.
Catholic Social Teaching link:St Paul encourages us to live out Solidarity, reminding us that we are one global family called to share God’s love with others.
Year 6 – St Joan of Arc
Feast Day: 30 MayPatron Saint of Courage and Young People
St Joan of Arc was chosen for Year 6 because she showed great courage, faith and determination from a young age. She trusted in God and used her voice to bring about change.
Catholic Social Teaching link:St Joan of Arc reflects Participation and Human Dignity, reminding us that every person has a voice, unique gifts and the ability to make a difference.
Living as a Community of Saints
Our class saints remind us that we are all called to follow Jesus and live lives of love and service. Through their examples, our children are encouraged to put Catholic Social Teaching into action and become compassionate, courageous and faithful members of our school and wider community.
Charity Work
Serving Our Community Through Charity and Action
At St Philomena’s Catholic Primary School, our mission calls us to serve our community by following the example of Jesus through love, compassion and generosity. We believe that faith is lived out through action, and that every member of our school community has a part to play in caring for others.
Our approach to charity is rooted in the principles of Catholic Social Teaching. We encourage our children to recognise the dignity of every person, show compassion towards those in need and understand that service is not only about giving money. Charity is also expressed through kindness, sharing, prayer, time, friendship and practical support.
We are mindful of the many requests placed upon families and our wider community, and we aim to support charitable causes in a thoughtful and meaningful way. Our focus is on helping children understand why we give, who we are supporting and how even small acts of love can make a difference.
Throughout the year, our school community supports a range of charities and causes. Our Lenten Walk raises money for the Catholic Children’s Society, helping children to understand the importance of supporting others facing difficult circumstances. Through our pre-loved uniform initiative, we support families within our own school community while promoting sustainability and care for creation.
We take part in community and national events such as the Greenwich Mini Marathon, raising funds for a local hospice, Children in Need, the Poppy Appeal and our Christmas charity jumper day. These opportunities help children see that they are connected to a wider community and can make a positive difference beyond our school.
We are proud to support CAFOD and to help children develop a sense of global responsibility by learning about the lives of people around the world. Our Harvest collection allows us to share our blessings with local food banks, supporting those in our local area who may need additional help.
Our service also extends to acts of kindness that do not involve fundraising. Following our Crowning of Mary celebration, children share flowers with residents in local care homes, bringing joy and building relationships with members of our wider community. Children also take part in prayer, environmental projects and everyday acts of kindness that reflect Jesus’ call to love and serve others.
Through all of these experiences, our children learn that they have the ability to make a difference. At St Philomena’s, we strive to nurture hearts that are generous, compassionate and ready to serve — living out our mission by caring for one another and our wider community.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Philomena's Catholic Primary School - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome to St Philomena’s Catholic Primary School
It is a great pleasure to welcome you to St Philomena’s Catholic Primary School.
For almost two centuries, St Philomena’s Catholic Primary School has been at the heart of our village community. Founded in 1836, we are immensely proud of our rich heritage and the enduring traditions that have shaped our school, whilst remaining firmly committed to providing a forward thinking education for every child entrusted to our care.
Nestled amongst beautiful green spaces, our school offers a tranquil setting in which children thrive both spiritually and academically. Our pupils, staff and families are united by a shared commitment to our Catholic values and to the pursuit of excellence, creating the distinctive sense of community that lies at the heart of our school. We are fortunate to work closely with our families, parish and wider community, recognising the important partnership between home and school in supporting every child to thrive.
At St Philomena's, we believe that childhood should be cherished and that every pupil should experience learning in a joyful and inspiring environment. Our children are happy, confident and curious, developing a genuine enthusiasm for learning as they grow in knowledge, understanding and self-belief. Alongside classroom learning, our children enjoy a rich and varied programme of experiences, including prayer and worship, sport, the creative arts, educational visits and opportunities to develop their talents, pursue new interests and make a meaningful contribution to our school and wider community.
We hope our website gives you a glimpse into the outstanding school community we are so proud of and the many opportunities our children have to pursue excellence, develop respect for others and serve our community.
It is a privilege to lead St Philomena's, and I look forward to welcoming you to our school.
With every blessing,
Mrs AndersonHeadteacher

pageCache.text:
Governors
Governing Body
Who We Are
The Governors of St Philomena’s Catholic Primary School are volunteers who give their time, knowledge and experience to support the school and its pupils.
The Governing Body works collectively to provide strategic leadership and oversight of the school. Our central aim is the welfare, education and achievement of all pupils, within the Catholic ethos and mission of the school.All governors are expected to act in the best interests of the school and its pupils. Governors work as a corporate team and accept collective responsibility for decisions made by the Governing Body.
How We Are Selected and Who We Represent
Governors are appointed or elected through different categories, in accordance with the school’s Instrument of Government. These include Foundation Governors, Parent Governors and Staff Governors.
Although governors may be appointed or elected through different routes, all governors have the same core responsibility to act in the best interests of the school and its pupils.
The Governing Body works closely with the Headteacher and school leaders to provide effective strategic oversight and challenge.
The Role of the Headteacher
The Headteacher is responsible for the day-to-day management and leadership of the school, including:
the day-to-day management of the school;
the educational performance of the school; and
The Role of Governors
The Governing Body provides strategic leadership and oversight of the school.
Governors are responsible for determining, monitoring and reviewing the policies, plans, targets and procedures within which the school operates.
Governors fulfil these responsibilities through Governing Body meetings, committee meetings, school visits, working parties, training and discussions with the Headteacher and other school leaders.
The Governing Body’s work is focused on supporting the school to provide a high-quality education and to raise the educational achievement and wellbeing of all pupils.
Effective Governance
The Governing Body aims to:
monitor the progress and achievement of pupils;
ensure that safeguarding remains a priority; and
Commitment, Confidentiality and Conduct
Being a school governor involves a significant commitment of time, energy and responsibility.
Governors attend regular Governing Body and committee meetings and may also take part in working parties, training, school visits and other activities.
Governors are expected to read papers and correspondence in preparation for meetings and to undertake appropriate training to develop and maintain the knowledge and skills required for effective governance.
Governors must maintain confidentiality where required and must comply with the Governing Body’s Code of Conduct and relevant school policies.
Governors may express their views freely during meetings and are expected to contribute constructively to discussion. Once a decision has been made collectively, governors support and uphold that decision.
Governors are expected to declare relevant interests and to manage any conflicts of interest appropriately.
The Catholic Governor
Foundation Governors have a particular responsibility to support and uphold the Catholic character and mission of the school.
All governors contribute to ensuring that pupils and staff experience a strong Catholic Christian environment in which faith, learning and service are closely connected.
The Governing Body ensures that Religious Education and the liturgical celebration of Catholic life remain an important part of the school’s strategic work.
Catholic governors undertake appropriate training relating to their responsibilities and contribute to the development of the school’s Catholic ethos.
The Governing Body seeks to ensure that every child is supported to develop their God-given talents to the highest possible level and is encouraged to use those talents in the service of others and in building the Kingdom of God.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Philomena's Catholic Primary School - Clubs
pageCache.text:
Clubs
Extra-Curricular and Enrichment Offer
Our Commitment to Personal Development
At St Philomena’s Catholic School, we believe that education extends beyond the classroom. Our extensive offer reflects our commitment to Strive for Excellence, Act with Respect and Serve Our Community. We strive for excellence by providing a wide range of opportunities that enable pupils to develop their gifts, talents and passions. We act with respect by creating an inclusive environment where every pupil is valued, encouraged and supported to participate. We serve our community by ensuring that enrichment opportunities are accessible to all pupils, with many clubs offered free of charge where possible, removing barriers and ensuring that every child can benefit from the opportunities available.
Through our enrichment programme, pupils develop character, confidence, resilience, cultural awareness, leadership and a sense of responsibility towards others. They are encouraged to explore new experiences, develop their individual strengths and make a positive contribution to the school and wider community.
Our commitment is that every pupil should have the opportunity to flourish academically, spiritually, socially and personally through a rich and ambitious programme of enrichment.
Our Enrichment Strands
Art and Culture
We provide opportunities for pupils to develop creativity, appreciate different cultures and express themselves through artistic experiences.
Our opportunities include:
• Art Club• Choir• Rocksteady• Drama Club• Dance Club• Music tuition• Creative writing• Cultural celebrations and events• Theatre visits and performances
Civic Engagement
We encourage pupils to understand their role within the school, parish and wider community, developing compassion, responsibility and a desire to serve others.
Examples of opportunities include:
• School Council• Chaplaincy groups• Charity fundraising• Community projects• Pupil leadership opportunities• Eco Warriors ( The Green Team)• Peer mentoring• Links with local organisations and parish communities
Nature
Pupils are given opportunities to develop an appreciation of creation, sustainability and their responsibility for caring for the environment.
Examples of opportunities include:
• Gardening Club• Wildlife projects• Recycling initiatives• Outdoor learning activities• Forest Education activities• Environmental awareness projects
Outdoor and Adventure
We provide experiences that develop resilience, teamwork, independence and confidence through outdoor challenges.
Examples of opportunities include:
• Residential trips• Orienteering• Outdoor learning• Team-building challenges
Sport and Physical Development
We promote healthy lifestyles, teamwork, perseverance and enjoyment through a wide range of sporting opportunities.
Examples of opportunities include:
• Football• Netball• Gymnastics• Dance• Competitions and tournaments
Developing Life Skills
We support pupils in developing the knowledge, skills and confidence needed for life beyond school.
Examples of opportunities include:
• Cooking Club• First Aid training• Financial education • Enterprise projects• Public speaking• Debate clubs• Study skills• Leadership programmes• Careers and aspiration activities
Impact
Through our enrichment offer, pupils are supported to develop confidence, resilience, independence and respect for others. The wide range of opportunities available enables pupils to discover and develop their talents, contribute positively to their community and live out our mission of striving for excellence, acting with respect and serving others.
Wraparound Care
Our Wraparound Care provision offers a safe, welcoming and nurturing environment for children before and after the school day. We aim to provide a warm and homely setting in which children feel happy, secure and well cared for.
Breakfast Club7:45am – 8:50am
Our Breakfast Club provides children with a calm and enjoyable start to the school day. A healthy breakfast is provided, followed by opportunities for children to socialise with their friends and enjoy a selection of quiet and purposeful activities before the school day begins.
After-School Club3:20pm – 5:45pm
Our After-School Club provides a relaxed and welcoming environment in which children can unwind at the end of the school day. Children may enjoy a variety of activities, including play, reading, creative pursuits and time with friends.
Healthy food and refreshments are provided during the session.
Our Wraparound Care provision offers families the reassurance that their children are cared for in a safe, supportive and stimulating environment beyond the school day.

pageCache.text:
Curriculum Approach
Curriculum Intent, Implementation and Impact Statement
Curriculum Intent
At St Philomena’s, we are committed to providing an ambitious, broad and enriching curriculum which enables every child to achieve their full potential academically, spiritually, socially and personally. Rooted in our Catholic faith, our curriculum places Christ at the centre of all that we do. We nurture children who strive for and achieve excellence, act with respect and serve their community, making a positive contribution to the wider world.
Our curriculum is designed to provide all children with the knowledge, skills and understanding they need to succeed. It is carefully planned and sequenced so that children build a rich body of knowledge over time. New learning builds upon prior knowledge, allowing children to make meaningful connections, develop deeper understanding and apply their learning with increasing independence. Through each subject, children develop the essential knowledge and skills needed to make strong progress, achieve high standards and prepare for future success.
St Philomena’s takes pride in providing a highly inclusive environment where all children are supported and challenged to achieve their very best. Through carefully adapted teaching, appropriate support and consistently high expectations, all children, including those with additional needs and those from different starting points, are enabled to access an ambitious curriculum, make strong progress and achieve highly.
Our curriculum develops the knowledge, understanding and cultural capital required for children to succeed. Our ambition is that every child leaves St Philomena’s with the academic knowledge, confidence and skills required to succeed at the next stage of their education and beyond. Through our commitment to excellence, children are equipped to achieve their ambitions and make a positive contribution to society.
Curriculum Implementation
Our curriculum is coherently planned and sequenced to ensure that children acquire the knowledge, skills and understanding required for future learning. Subject leaders carefully design progression pathways which identify how knowledge and skills develop across each year group and ensure that learning builds systematically over time.
Continuing Professional Development for all staff is a priority to ensure that teachers develop strong subject knowledge and deliver the highest standards across the entire curriculum. Teaching is inspirational, purposeful and consistently ambitious. Lessons are meticulously planned using skilful assessment of prior learning to ensure that teaching is precisely matched to children’s needs. Teachers use expert questioning, rich opportunities for discussion and purposeful speaking and listening activities to deepen understanding, develop vocabulary and encourage children to think critically.
The learning ethos within lessons is exceptional. Children are motivated, engaged and confident learners who demonstrate curiosity, resilience and a willingness to challenge themselves. Teachers create classrooms where all children feel valued, supported and inspired to achieve their very best.
We recognise the importance of securing knowledge in children’s long-term memory. Retrieval practice is embedded across the curriculum to strengthen recall and help children make connections between new and prior learning. Teachers regularly revisit key knowledge, vocabulary and concepts through questioning, review activities and opportunities for children to explain and apply their understanding.
We use Rosenshine’s Principles of Instruction to support effective teaching and learning. Teachers:
Assessment is an integral part of our curriculum approach. Teachers continually assess children’s understanding and use this information to adapt teaching, address misconceptions and provide appropriate support or challenge. Assessment enables teachers to identify next steps and ensures that all children make progress from their individual starting points.
Reading is prioritised throughout our curriculum. We aim to develop confident, fluent readers who develop a love of reading and recognise the importance of reading as a gateway to learning. High-quality texts are carefully selected to enrich children’s vocabulary, knowledge and understanding of the wider world.
Our curriculum provides meaningful opportunities for children to develop cultural capital through enrichment experiences, including visits, visitors, the arts, sporting opportunities and community involvement. These experiences enable children to develop confidence, broaden their horizons and understand their role within the local, national and global community.
Through our curriculum, children are encouraged to live out our values by achieving excellence, showing respect and serving their school and wider community. They are given opportunities to develop leadership, responsibility and independence, preparing them to become active, compassionate and responsible citizens.

Curriculum Impact
The impact of our curriculum is evident in the exceptional outcomes achieved by our children. They develop secure, deep knowledge and skills, achieve highly from their starting points and produce work of a consistently high standard. Our children are confident, independent and resilient learners who are able to apply their knowledge creatively across a range of contexts. They leave St Philomena’s exceptionally well prepared for the next stage of their education, with the ambition, skills and confidence to succeed.
The effectiveness of our curriculum is rigorously evaluated through a rich range of evidence, including pupil voice, book scrutiny, lesson visits, learning walks, assessment information, curriculum reviews and discussions with staff, children and parents. This enables leaders and teachers to continually refine and enhance provision, ensuring that the curriculum remains ambitious, inclusive and responsive to the needs of every child.
Our broad and carefully sequenced curriculum provides children with the powerful knowledge, academic foundations and transferable skills needed to excel. It extends beyond the classroom by developing cultural capital, broadening children’s experiences and nurturing curiosity, creativity and a lifelong love of learning. Through exposure to rich texts, diverse perspectives, the arts, sporting opportunities, visits, visitors and meaningful experiences, children develop confidence, aspiration and a deeper understanding of the wider world. They recognise their own potential and understand how they can make a positive contribution to society.
Rooted in our Catholic values, our curriculum develops children’s character alongside their academic success. They learn to respect and celebrate difference, show compassion, serve others and make a positive contribution to their community and the wider world. Children leave St Philomena’s as knowledgeable, articulate and empathetic young people, equipped with the confidence, resilience and moral purpose to achieve their aspirations and succeed throughout their lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Philomena's Catholic Primary School - History
pageCache.text:
History
St Philomena’s Catholic Primary School History
c.1856 – The beginnings of Catholic education in St Mary Cray
A Catholic school was established at Lawrence’s Yard, St Mary Cray by Dr Todd, formerly President of the Royal Irish Society and a respected writer on St Patrick and the early Irish Church.
This was a private Catholic school, founded before the Education Act of 1870, and represents the earliest known roots of Catholic education in the area and the beginnings of what later became St Joseph’s Catholic School.
1934 – Arrival of the Sisters of Charity
The Sisters of Charity of Our Lady, Mother of Mercy, a religious community originating in Holland, came to St Mary Cray.
Marion Bailey’s family moved with them. Her parents helped support the convent, with her father working as a handyman and maintenance manager and her mother assisting in the convent kitchen. Marion later became one of the school’s longest-serving teachers, teaching for around 40 years.
1935 – St Philomena’s Convent School opens
St Philomena’s Convent School opened on the site of the present school.
It was a private Catholic school, run and taught by the Sisters of Charity, who educated generations of children in the parish.
1936 – Expansion of St Joseph’s Catholic School
Sister Clare McHugh became Headmistress of St Joseph’s RC School. She began fundraising and expanding the school buildings before the outbreak of World War II.
1941 – Wartime bombing and temporary relocation
During the bombing of London and the South East, the St Joseph’s school building was destroyed.
The pupils temporarily moved to St Philomena’s Convent Hall, where lessons continued and Mass was also celebrated until new parish facilities became available.
1942 – Rowlands Manor becomes a school site
Rowlands Manor, formerly the home of the Heckstall-Smith family near Reynolds Cross, was made available to the parish.
It was used as a school site, particularly for the older pupils.
1940s – Evacuation during World War II
As bombing intensified, many St Joseph’s children were evacuated to Porthmadog, Wales, where they were billeted with Catholic families until the end of the war.
Sister Clare and other nuns continued teaching pupils in temporary accommodation, including a prefabricated hall transferred from another Diocesan school in Dartford.
1945 – Sister Veronica becomes Headmistress
Sister Veronica took over as Headmistress and continued developing St Joseph’s, which remained an all-age school for children aged 5 to 14.
1949 – New Church Hall (Frawley Centre)
The Church Hall was completed, providing an important meeting place for parish and school life.
1958 – Temporary classrooms
The Diocese of Southwark rented huts from the London Borough of Bromley at Rectory Paddock, Main Road, St Paul’s Cray, as temporary classrooms.
1960s – Changes to Catholic education
With the introduction of secondary schools in the London Borough of Bromley, St Joseph’s gradually became a primary school, with older pupils transferring to Catholic secondary schools.
1965 – New leadership
Sister Veronica retired. She was followed by Head Teachers George Parker and later Roger Gilchrist Kelly.
1970 – Veronica Shelley-Pearce becomes Headmistress
Veronica Shelley Pearce (née McCullagh) became Headmistress.
At this time, St Joseph’s was housed in sixteen Nissen huts at Riverside, St Mary Cray.
1971 – St Philomena’s Convent School closes
After 36 years as a private Catholic school, St Philomena’s Convent School closed in July 1971.
October 1972 – The move to the present site
During the October half term, St Joseph’s RC Primary School moved to the former grounds of St Philomena’s High School.
The school was renamed: St Philomena’s Roman Catholic Primary School
This brought together the traditions and memories of both St Joseph’s and St Philomena’s.
1980 – The convent building closes
The old convent building was demolished.
The Sisters of Charity moved to two houses in Southborough Lane, Petts Wood, continuing their community life.
c.2000 – New Head Teacher
Mary Riley succeeded Veronica Shelley Pearce as Head Teacher.
2012 – New Head Teacher
Veronica Maher became Head Teacher following Mary Riley’s retirement.
2014 – Becoming an Academy
St Philomena’s Roman Catholic Primary School converted to academy status on 1 October 2014, becoming a single-academy trust.
The school’s official name changed to St Philomena’s Catholic Primary School, while continuing its Roman Catholic identity and connection with the Archdiocese of Southwark.
2014 – Fr Cyriacus Okafor joins the parish
In 2014, Fr Cyriacus Okafor joined Our Lady of the Crays, St Mary Cray, beginning his ministry with the parish and strengthening the close relationship between the parish and St Philomena’s Catholic Primary School.
2020 – COVID-19 pandemic and remote learning
During the COVID-19 pandemic, St Philomena’s moved to remote learning during lockdown before reopening with safety measures in place, including support for key workers’ children.
2022 – 50 years
In 2022, St Philomena’s marked 50 years since moving to its present site, following the relocation of St Joseph’s RC Primary School in 1972 and the creation of St Philomena’s RC Primary School.
2025 – Joining the St Oscar Romero Catholic Academy Trust
Directed by the Diocese of Southwark to join a Catholic Multi-Academy Trust, St Philomena’s became part of the St Oscar Romero Catholic Academy Trust.
2026 – New Head Teacher
After many years of dedicated leadership, Veronica Maher retired as Head Teacher of St Philomena’s Catholic Primary School. Stacey Anderson was appointed as the new Head Teacher.
Today
St Philomena’s Catholic Primary School continues to build on a long and proud history of Catholic education in St Mary Cray, bringing together the legacy of St Joseph’s and St Philomena’s while preparing future generations of children for the years ahead.
